scope: Qwen3.5-4B ordinary text inference on one RTX 5090; existing paths remeasured.
privacy: Allowlisted metrics and hashes only; prompt text, input/output token arrays, hostnames, private paths and commands omitted.

model.timing_scope: Synchronous native packed generation; no HTTP, queue or tokenizer time. Prefill ends before sampling; first-token-ready includes one argmax and sync. Decode starts after that sync; no per-token sync. Host token copy excluded.
model.protocol: One model load; full-shape generation warmup per backend/case; cyclic backend order across rounds; fixed-count greedy ignoring EOS; compare free-running tokens with same-round, same-shape reference, not HF

cross_batch.scope: Same round and variant; identical prompt prefix across different packed batch sizes. Free-running outputs; not operator-level attribution.

limitations: B1 input lengths are prefixes of one synthetic sequence with a 14-token period; these are not independent semantic tasks.
Repeated runs are repeated requests, not independent correctness samples or model quality scores.
Native generation is not HTTP TTFT, TPOT, or serving throughput. B32 is direct model execution only.
P128/B8/B32 candidate parity failures prevent global correctness acceptance.
Each configuration is internally repeatable; the reference itself is sensitive to batch changes.
Allocated memory includes resident weights; reserved memory depends on process allocation history.
CUDA event intervals can include host launch gaps; these are not pure kernel latency.
Microbench complete is a timing status, not independent proof of numerical correctness.
77 tests include a few CPU fallback/argument checks; they do not establish all model shapes.
GDN Q/K head expansion is outside the microbenchmark timing.

sm120.protocol: 3 rounds; eager includes Python and allocation; graph_us excludes host launch gaps; all variants checked against portable tile32/warp4
limitations: Numerical comparison is against portable tile32/warp4, not full-model greedy.
Graph operator gains at T1 did not improve complete wrapper latency.

profiles.method: CPU external-id / launch correlation to containing module; all GPU kernel streams; profiler timing is diagnostic
limitations: Profiler timings are structural diagnostics, not formal benchmark latency.
Kernel sum, busy union, and GPU event span have different meanings; no Nsight Compute hardware counters were collected.
Percentiles are calculated per round, then averaged across three rounds; not pooled request P95.
Only mixed-to-overlap had all 48 matching outputs. GDN HTTP is not correctness accepted.
GDN first rounds were slower and one C4 request changed output across repeats; no round was discarded.
Four warmup requests do not establish warmup coverage of C8 and every mixed shape.
AIPerf SPEED is a separate nine-request C1 workload with natural EOS; its ITL differs from custom-client TPOT.
Cancellation and release checks are finite tests, not evidence of long-duration stability.

graph.scope: B1/prefix16, reference GDN and norm, math SDPA; isolated decode wrapper, not HTTP.
graph.timing_scope: forward_packed including graph load/replay/commit; state cloning and token selection excluded; events and synchronized wall per call
